title: The San Francisco minstrel show job, and meeting Susie
summary: Howard recounts being fired after two or three weeks from a minstrel show in San Francisco, with Alma Hightower, and says he met Susie there.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: We lost the part--because of the interruption and the microphone--we lost the part about the minstrel show that you played with in San Francisco. Something happened to the microphone connection on that one.
The minstrel show?
Uh-huh.
Who, me?
Yeh. That's what you told us last time. In San Francisco? In the '30s, I think it was, wasn't it?
Yes.
(chuckle) Yeah, I remember that. But I lost the job, too. (laughter)
And how'd that happen?
Huh?
How did that happen?
The man just fired us.
Oh.
Yep, a lot'a that.
No reason?
He say we couldn't play good enough.
Oh.
that was all.
Just tryin'. Give it a chance, you know. But I didn't care. It didn't bother me as long as I had that horn in my hand. I knew I'd be blowin' some-place.
Did you stay in San Francisco then or did you come back to L.A.?
No, I worked in San Francisco, believe it or not. Worked in San Francisco.
On another job, besides the minstrel show? What--where else did you work there, then?
I can't think of the name of that job--who the people were, or anybody. I went and got Alma Hightower --took her with me (chuckle).
Hmmm.
I knew that.
Uh-huh.
Those things don't stick with you, like that, so long. It's kinda' hard, little lady. I'm sorry.
You mentioned at an earlier time that you gave Lionel Hampton his first job here in Los Angeles.
I did.
And then later, you worked in--
You know where it was?
Where was that?
Down on --what's-er-name street?-- Oh, for God's sake--
Was it Main Street?
No, it wadn't Main Street.
Broadway? They had some clubs (Inaudible) down there.

Could've been Broadway. It could have been. I have to stop and think about it awhile. It'll come to me. It's a long time--long time, and I was younger, now I'm older, now I hadn't got as much sense as I had then.
Oh, you seem to have pretty good sense.
No, I don't.
You're doing very well.

I don't have as much sense as I did have. Once I was little, boy, I was a humdinger. Smart, but I'm not no more. Just can't put myself together. I wisht I could. See, in that band up there, I was playin' at the--I'm tryin' to think of the name of the name of the place where Alma was playin'. You should know it; she's your cousin. Isn't she some relation to you?
No. I wish we were, but--she's somebody I admired for a long time. I've admired her for a long time.
You admire her?
Oh, yes, because of all she's done. And, you know, she's a fabulous lady. But I never got a chance to work with her or anything like that.
You didn't?
No, I'd seen her, you know, briefly. But that's about it. I knew who she was and what she was doing,
But you were fortunate --you had a chance to meet her, personally and work with her.
Oh, yeah, I worked with her.
Uh-huh. But, no, she's a relation of Alton Redd. And (unintelligible) naturally Vi Redd.
Yep.
Uh-huh. But you mentioned, when you were doing the minstrel, that she was with you in the minstrel show?
Yeah, in the minstrel show.
So, how long did the job last before they fired you. Do you know? Did you work a week? Two weeks?
Oh, worked about --yeah, about two weeks. Three weeks. Two or three weeks.
Yeah. You said the proprietor, the boss of your job decided he didn't like your music?
Didn't like what?
He didn't like what you were playing?
No, he didn't like the music, no.
But you think the band was good?
Yeah, the band was good, I thought.
He just wanted something different?
That's all. He wanted something different.
Yeah. And after that, did you stay with minstrel shows, or did you come back to Los Angeles to do something else?
I came back to Los Angeles. Uh-huh. That's where I met Susie, up there.
You met Susie in San Francisco?
Yeah (laughter).
Oh, yeah? It's all--see--it's coming back to you.
(laughter)
(laughter) Comin' back.
Yeah. Well, that's the way.
That's where I met her.
